anyOf.description: Qualified snake_case noun phrase of at least two words: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters and digits, with each further word after a single underscore (`analysis_target`, never bare `target`).

items.description: Snake_case noun phrase of at least two words, or a listed single-word exemption.

reads.description: Session variables this activity consults and does not produce: gate and routing conditions, loop collections, prose interpolations, and the bound techniques' inputs it does not supply itself. A name written by an earlier step of the same activity is local and not declared here.

type.description: Declared variable type. A value written to the session, through a checkpoint `setVariable` effect or a reported variable change, is checked against it; a mismatch is stored as written with a warning, and a `{name}` template value is exempt.

description.description: Meaning and intended use of the variable.

items.description: Allowed string value for the variable.

values.description: Complete set of values the variable admits: nonempty, without repeats, and declared only on a `string` variable. A declared `defaultValue` must be one of them. A value written outside the set is stored as written with a warning, and a `{name}` template value is exempt.

defaultValue.description: Initial value, present from the start of every session and child session. Do not gate a defaulted variable with `exists` or `notExists`: the variable is always present, so the gate is constant, and `check:variable-model` rejects it.

required.description: Marks the variable as expected to be set; no check reads it.

items.description: Variable declaration with type, allowed values, and an optional initial value.

writes.description: Declarations for the session variables this activity writes: its bound techniques' outputs (under their identifier or the step binding's remap target), its checkpoint `setVariable` effects, its `set` action targets, and the item variable each of its loops binds. Contributed to the variable set of every workflow whose graph includes the activity, `defaultValue` included.

variables.description: Session variable names required by this activity and declarations for the variables it writes.

maxChars.description: Maximum characters per step technique included with the activity; zero excludes all step techniques.

bundleTechniques.description: Optional character limit for inline step techniques.

id.description: Step identifier, unique within its step list (the top-level steps, or one loop body). A duplicate excludes its activity from the load; in a routine file, it fails the load of any workflow that reads that routine. Defaults to the last `::` segment of the technique reference; the one step kind whose id may be omitted.

name.description: Technique reference: `group::technique`, a bare technique name, or `workflow::group::technique`.

additionalProperties.description: Variable name, literal value, or template expression for an input.

inputs.description: Input identifiers mapped to a source: the name of a session variable to read under that input, a literal, or a `{template}` expression. Declared only for inputs whose source differs from the same-name variable or the declared default.

additionalProperties.description: Workflow variable name for the output.

outputs.description: Output identifiers mapped to the workflow variable each value is written to. Declared only where that name differs from the output identifier.

anyOf.description: Technique reference with input and output bindings.

technique.description: Technique reference, or an object with `name` and optional `inputs` and `outputs` bindings.

action.description: Action for the executing agent to perform; a `set` value reaches the session when the agent reports it.

target.description: Variable name or other target of the action.

value.description: Value assigned or supplied by the action.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this action does

condition.description: Condition that must be true for this action to execute

items.description: Action with an optional target, value, message, and condition.

actions.description: Actions associated with the technique step.

when.description: Entry gate: the step runs only when this expression holds. On a checkpoint step, `condition`, not `when`, makes the checkpoint dismissible.

required.description: Declare `false` for an optional step; omission means the step is required, and `true` is rejected.

condition.description: Structured entry condition. Prefer `when` for a step gate. On a checkpoint step, `condition` is the only gate that makes the checkpoint dismissible: when it is false, the checkpoint may be dismissed as not met, selecting no option and no exit.

anyOf.description: Step that invokes a technique with optional actions and entry conditions.

id.description: Step identifier, unique within its step list (the top-level steps, or one loop body). A duplicate excludes its activity from the load; in a routine file, it fails the load of any workflow that reads that routine.

actions.description: Control actions; may be empty for marker steps.

anyOf.description: Control step with optional actions and entry conditions.

id.description: Checkpoint identifier, unique within its step list (the top-level steps, or one loop body). A duplicate excludes its activity from the load; in a routine file, it fails the load of any workflow that reads that routine, and the key its recorded responses replay under on resume.

additionalProperties.description: Value assigned to the named variable.

setVariable.description: Variable assignments applied when this option is selected. Each value is checked against the variable's declared type and value set, and a mismatch is stored as written with a warning; a `{name}` template value passes through unchecked.

exit.description: Exit of the owning activity this option selects: a name from its `exits`, never an activity identifier. An option naming an exit its activity does not declare fails the workflow load. Omitted for an ad hoc checkpoint, which has no declared exits.

effect.description: Variable assignments and activity exit associated with the choice.

items.description: Checkpoint choice and its associated effects.

defaultOption.description: Identifier of one of this checkpoint's options, taken when no person answers. Declared together with `autoAdvanceMs`: the pair makes the checkpoint soft, and a hard checkpoint declares neither.

autoAdvanceMs.description: Positive waiting interval in milliseconds before `defaultOption` may be selected automatically; declared together with `defaultOption`.

anyOf.description: User decision at a defined position in the activity steps.

id.description: Step identifier, unique within its step list (the top-level steps, or one loop body). A duplicate excludes its activity from the load; in a routine file, it fails the load of any workflow that reads that routine.

loopType.description: Iteration over a collection (`forEach`), with a pre-test (`while`), or with a post-test (`doWhile`).

continueWhile.description: Continuation condition required for `while` and `doWhile` loops and absent for `forEach` loops.

variable.description: Current-item variable bound each iteration of a `forEach` loop; absent for `while` and `doWhile` loops.

over.description: Collection a `forEach` loop iterates: a variable name or a dotted path into one; absent for `while` and `doWhile` loops.

breakCondition.description: Condition that ends a `forEach` loop before the next item; absent for `while` and `doWhile` loops.

steps.description: The loop body, a nested ordered list of steps.

anyOf.description: Loop over a collection or until a continuation test fails, entered when its `when` expression holds.

id.description: Step identifier, unique within its step list (the top-level steps, or one loop body). A duplicate excludes its activity from the load; in a routine file, it fails the load of any workflow that reads that routine, and the prefix every identifier in the routine body carries once spliced in.

routine.description: Routine reference in `[namespace::]name` form. The namespace is a directory name, or the path from the corpus root reaching it. A qualified name resolves in that namespace only; a bare name resolves against the referring activity's source workflow, then `meta`. The last segment is the routine and every segment before it is the namespace, since a routine name has no group grammar.

additionalProperties.description: Literal argument or braced host-variable reference.

with.description: Routine input identifiers mapped to arguments: a braced value (`{host_variable}`) references a host variable, and any other value is a literal. An input left unbound takes its declared default, then the host variable of the same name; a `kind: technique` input left unbound with no default, or an argument naming no declared input, excludes the referring activity from the load.

additionalProperties.description: Session variable name for the routine output.

outputs.description: Routine output identifiers mapped to session variable names. An output left unbound produces no write; only an output declared `optional: true` may be left unbound. Any other unbound output, or a binding naming no declared output, excludes the referring activity from the load.

anyOf.description: Routine invocation with argument and output bindings, entered when its `when` expression holds.

items.description: Step selected by `kind`; its guidance lives in the bound technique.

steps.description: Ordered steps, with checkpoints and loops at their positions in the sequence.

id.description: Kebab-case outcome name, unique within the activity and distinct from a destination activity identifier.

when.description: Expression selecting this exit, in the same dialect as a step `when`. Omitted on the default exit and on an exit only a checkpoint option selects.

isDefault.description: Declare `true` for the exit taken when no `when` matches and no checkpoint option selects an exit, including when a checkpoint is dismissed because its condition was not met. Required on exactly one exit of an activity with two or more exits; `false` is rejected.

immediate.description: Declare `true` so that selecting this exit at a checkpoint ends the step sequence there, and the remaining steps do not run. Omission records the exit when chosen and takes it when the steps finish; `false` is rejected.

items.description: Named activity outcome with optional selection and completion conditions.

exits.description: Named outcomes, one of which the activity takes when its steps end. Every exit is bound to a destination in the workflow `graph`, and an unbound exit fails the workflow load. An activity with two or more exits declares exactly one `isDefault`. Omission makes the activity terminal.

workflow.description: ID of the workflow to trigger

description.description: When and why to trigger this workflow.

items.description: Name of a context variable to pass to the child workflow.

passContext.description: Context variable names to pass to the child workflow.

items.description: Child workflow reference and context to pass to it.

triggers.description: Child workflows to start from this activity.

items.description: Expected result of successful activity completion.

outcome.description: Expected outcomes of successful activity completion.

required.description: Whether this activity is required in the workflow

items.description: Rule or constraint for this activity.

rules.description: Activity-level rules and constraints that agents must follow

artifactPrefix.description: Numeric artifact filename prefix, taken from the activity filename (`02` from `02-design-philosophy.yaml`); omitted from authored activity definitions.

activity.description: Activity with ordered steps; its artifacts are declared by the techniques its steps bind.

whenExpression.description: Inline boolean expression in the `when` dialect, evaluated against the current session variables. Grammar: `orExpr := andExpr ('||' andExpr)*`; `andExpr := unary ('&&' unary)*`; `unary := '!' unary | primary`; `primary := IDENT | comparison | 'true' | 'false' | '(' orExpr ')'`; `comparison := IDENT ('==' | '!=' | '>' | '<' | '>=' | '<=') literal`. Precedence, tightest first: `()`, comparisons, `!`, `&&`, `||`; so `!a == b` reads as `!(a == b)`, and a negated left side of a comparison is not expressible. Mixing `&&` and `||` at the same nesting depth requires parentheses, so grouping is always explicit: `(a && b) || c`, never `a && b || c`. An IDENT is a variable name or a dotted path into one (`execution_plan.status`): a letter or underscore, then letters, digits, underscores and dots. A literal is `true`, `false`, `null`, a single- or double-quoted string (a backslash escapes the next character), an integer with an optional leading `-`, or a bare word, which is a string (`analysis_type == completion`). Decimals are not literals. A bare IDENT holds when its value is truthy. A variable that is absent is undefined: it is falsy, `==` matches nothing (not even `null` or `false`), and `!=` matches every literal. `==` and `!=` compare strictly, without type coercion. `>`, `<`, `>=` and `<=` convert both sides to numbers and are false when either side is not a finite number. An expression that does not parse evaluates to false. Examples: `has_saved_state == true`, `remediation_round > 0`, `!is_review_mode`, `a == true && b != false`, `(a && b) || c`, `is_review_mode != true && (problem_complexity == "moderate" || problem_complexity == "complex")`.

type.description: Identifies a variable comparison or presence test.

variable.description: Variable name or dot-separated path to the value to test; a path through a missing or non-object segment reads as absent.

operator.description: Comparison or presence test applied to a variable. `==` and `!=` compare strictly, without type coercion. `>`, `<`, `>=` and `<=` compare numbers and numeric strings, and are false when either side is anything else. `exists` holds when the value is present and not null; `notExists` holds when it is absent or null.

value.description: Comparison value; unnecessary for `exists` and `notExists` tests.

anyOf.description: Comparison of a variable with a value, or a test of its presence.

conditions.description: At least two conditions that must all be true.

anyOf.description: Condition requiring every member to be true.

conditions.description: At least two conditions, one or more of which must be true.

anyOf.description: Condition requiring at least one member to be true.
Condition requiring its member to be false.

condition.description: Variable test or combination of conditions using `and`, `or`, or `not`.
